bear_case: There is a budget owner (DAWG, SOCOM, Navy PMS 406) and a requirement, but the FY27 request of $54.6B was marked at ~$1.0B by HASC, SASC and House appropriators; the AVO $100M is a prize ceiling with no public awards found; the obligated dollars located ($86M SOCOM, $87M Army task order) all went to Anduril; and the pain is still largely experimentation-stage (exercises, SOF trials, Gauntlet fielding). A startup's realistic revenue here is challenge/SBIR prototype money - consultancy drift into integration services for a prime.
strongest_single_argument: Every budget line that touches vehicle-agnostic orchestration is already routed either to Anduril through existing vehicles or to government-owned software (FANTOM Core, A-GRA, UMAA); there is no line a new entrant can address.
what_would_change_my_mind: Public AVO awards or a follow-on DAWG OTA going to a small non-incumbent vendor, or a FY27 appropriation with a dedicated vehicle-agnostic C2 line open to new entrants.
narrower_survivable_version: None within G25; adjacent autonomy conformance/T&E tooling sold to SOFWERX UxSAI, the JATF Autonomous Warfare Proving Ground or Drone Dominance vendors is a separate gap.

bear_case: Anduril Lattice is already the selected orchestration layer for DIU/Replicator (Nov 2024), SOCOM ($86M, Mar 2025) and the Army (enterprise agreement, Mar 2026), and holds a CCA mission-autonomy production option; Shield AI, Auterion (multi-manufacturer swarm demos, Gauntlet award), Applied Intuition/EpiSci, Collins, Palantir, AeroVironment and reportedly SpaceX/xAI compete for the same slot; the government's own kernels (FANTOM Core, A-GRA, UMAA, TAK) occupy the vendor-neutral position; every API a neutral layer needs is controlled by those vendors or the government; and switching cost for buyers already on Lattice is high while switching cost away from a startup adapter is zero.
strongest_single_argument: Incumbents do not need six months to add this - they already are it, and the neutral alternative is government-owned software that no one will pay a startup to replace.
what_would_change_my_mind: A formal DoD policy or NDAA provision mandating a government-owned, openly licensed orchestration interface with a funded third-party conformance program that explicitly procures from small vendors.
narrower_survivable_version: None for the orchestrator; a conformance/adapter tooling vendor that primes and government labs both use could coexist with incumbents but is not G25.

bear_case: A credible demo requires live heterogeneous vehicles across two domains, DDIL radio behavior, a DoDD 3000.09-compatible safety case and government interface specs (FANTOM Core, A-GRA, UMAA) that are CUI/ITAR; the product's core code is likely ITAR technical data or EAR 600-series, so the Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder may be unable to work on it without a licence and neither founder can be cleared today; $250k funds a simulation only (credible demo est. $2-5M); the AVO submission window closed 25 Jan 2026 and the challenge is described as for U.S.-based firms with production-approaching prototypes; and common-controller efforts have taken over a decade without reaching production.
strongest_single_argument: The thing that must be built to be credible - DDIL-tolerant multi-vehicle orchestration with lethal-tasking accountability - is exactly the thing this team cannot legally staff, cannot afford to test and cannot demo without military access.
evidence: S13 regulatory_access and technical_difficulty assessments (segment file, INFERENCE, MEDIUM)
what_would_change_my_mind: Export counsel opining that an open, simulation-first conformance kernel is EAR99/publicly available, plus a cleared U.S.-person co-founder or advisor with a SOCOM/Navy unmanned sponsor and access to range time.
narrower_survivable_version: Simulation-first, openly published conformance and T&E tooling (potentially publicly available and therefore outside ITAR - counsel) sold to labs and vendors; a different gap, and still LOW founder fit until a cleared U.S. lead joins.
